CEPNICI.name: Flailmen
CEPNICI.description: Hussite infantry with war flails. Crushing blow against armored troops.

lore.description: Armed peasants and townspeople forming the backbone of Hussite armies. The war flail, originally an agricultural tool, became a symbol of Hussite resistance. Flailmen were feared for their ferocity and ability to crush even the finest armor.
lore.equipment: War flail (reinforced with iron, often with iron spikes), short sword or dagger, helmet, light brigandine
lore.origin: Tábor, Hussite towns
lore.historicalNote: "They knew how to strike with flails so terribly that noble armor avoided them like the devil avoids the cross." - period chronicle

SUDLICNICI.name: Pikemen
SUDLICNICI.description: Infantry with pole weapons. Reach over allied units.

lore.description: Footmen armed with long pole weapons - pikes, bills, or halberds. Their reach allowed them to strike enemies over rows of comrades or over the edge of war wagons.
lore.equipment: Pike (pole weapon with blade and hook, 2-3 meters long), short knife, light helmet, quilted jacket
lore.origin: Town militia and rural levies
lore.historicalNote: "A good man with a pike can pull even a knight from his horse and pin him to the ground."

PAVEZNICI.name: Pavise Bearers
PAVEZNICI.description: Defenders with large pavises. Protect adjacent ranged units.

lore.description: Specialists in defense armed with large pavises - rectangular shields almost as tall as a man. They formed living walls protecting archers during loading and shooting.
lore.equipment: Pavise (large shield, often painted with Hussite symbols - chalice, goose), short sword or club, light armor
lore.origin: Specially trained defenders from town guilds
lore.historicalNote: "The pavise bearers stood like a wall, and behind them crossbows sang death to the Germans."

KOPINICI_HUSITI.name: Spearmen
KOPINICI_HUSITI.description: Infantry with long spears. Effective against cavalry.

lore.description: Footmen with long spears, specially trained for fighting cavalry. They formed defensive squares or lines that could stop even heavy knightly cavalry.
lore.equipment: Long spear (4-5 meters), short sword, light helmet, quilted jacket or brigandine
lore.origin: More experienced warriors from town and village militias
lore.historicalNote: "Stand firm, spears forward, and no knight shall defeat you!" - attributed to Jan Žižka

lore.description: Archers with crossbows, forming an important part of Hussite firepower. The crossbow was accurate and penetrating, capable of piercing even plate armor at medium range.
lore.equipment: Crossbow with steel bow, quiver with arrows (bolts), short sword or dagger, light armor
lore.origin: Townsmen and hunters
lore.historicalNote: "One crossbowman is worth ten men when he has time to reload."

lore.description: Elite gunners armed with primitive firearms - hand cannons and pistols. Their weapons were loud, inaccurate, but devastating at short range and causing panic among enemies and horses.
lore.equipment: Hand cannon or pistol (hand firearm), ignition supplies, gunpowder, lead balls, dagger
lore.origin: Specially trained warriors from craftsmen ranks (blacksmiths, bellmakers)
lore.historicalNote: "When the pistols thundered, horses panicked and knights fell from them like acorns from an oak."

lore.description: Heavy field guns capable of devastating area bombardment. Hussites were pioneers in using artillery in field battles, not just during sieges.
lore.equipment: Howitzer (short large-caliber gun), gunpowder, stone or iron balls, crew of 4-6 men
lore.origin: Guns manufactured in Hussite towns (Prague, Tábor). Crew consisted of specialists - gunners.
lore.historicalNote: "The howitzer struck enemy formations like the Lord's fist."

TARASNICE.name: Tarasnice
TARASNICE.description: Mobile gun. Can shoot after moving.

lore.description: Light mobile gun mounted on a cart or stretcher. The Tarasnice was a Hussite invention enabling fire support even during maneuvers.
lore.equipment: Tarasnice (light gun), gunpowder, smaller balls, crew of 2-3 men
lore.origin: Hussite invention combining firepower with mobility
lore.historicalNote: "The Tarasnice rode with the army like a faithful dog and barked at the enemy with lead."

VOZOVA_HRADBA.name: War Wagon
VOZOVA_HRADBA.description: Fortified wagon. Forms wagon fort with other wagons.

lore.description: The heart of Hussite military doctrine. Heavy peasant wagons modified for combat - reinforced with iron, with wooden shields on the sides, loopholes for shooters, and hooks for connecting. They formed a mobile fortress.
lore.equipment: The wagon itself (reinforced, with chains for connecting), crew includes driver, 2-4 shooters, 2-4 defenders with flails/pikes
lore.origin: Originally common peasant wagons modified for war. Hussites perfected their use to an art form.
lore.historicalNote: "The wagon fort is like a castle that goes with the army. And from that castle, death flies upon enemies of God's truth." - attributed to Jan Žižka

JIZDA_HUSITI.name: Light Cavalry
JIZDA_HUSITI.description: Fast cavalry for reconnaissance and pursuit.

lore.description: Hussite cavalry was always weaker than knightly cavalry, but fulfilled important tasks - reconnaissance, pursuit of fleeing enemies, and quick strikes on flanks.
lore.equipment: Light spears, swords, crossbows from horseback (some), light armor or just leather jacket
lore.origin: Gentry and wealthy townsmen who could afford horses. Also defectors from Catholic ranks.
lore.historicalNote: "Our cavalry cannot face knights, but can pursue them when they flee - and gladly does so!"

ZVED.name: Scout
ZVED.description: Light horseman for reconnaissance. Sees 6 hexes, can quickly retreat.

lore.description: Light riders specialized in reconnaissance, enemy tracking, and message delivery. They avoided combat and their main weapons were speed and keen eyes.
lore.equipment: Light sword or dagger, perhaps short crossbow, no armor or just leather jacket
lore.origin: Hunters, border guards, sons of peasants who could ride. Often knew the terrain better than anyone.
lore.historicalNote: "A good scout is like the captain's eyes. Without eyes, even the strongest army is blind."

lore.description: The elite of the medieval battlefield. A fully armored rider on an armored horse represented an unstoppable force - until they encountered Hussite wagons and firearms.
lore.equipment: Plate armor (full protection), lance, sword, heraldic shield, armored horse (often with chanfron)
lore.origin: Nobility from all over Europe - German, Hungarian, Polish, Burgundian knights. Some fought for faith, others for loot.
lore.historicalNote: "When a knight mounts his horse, there is no power under heaven that can stop him - except a wall of wagons and a rain of lead."

TEZKOODENCI.name: Men-at-Arms
TEZKOODENCI.description: Armored cavalry. Charge bonus when attacking from movement.

lore.description: Less armored cavalry than heavy knights, but still a formidable force. They often formed the second wave of attack or protected the flanks.
lore.equipment: Mail or partial plate armor, lance, sword, shield
lore.origin: Lower nobility, wealthy townsmen, experienced mercenaries with horses
lore.historicalNote: "They are not true knights, but sufficient for peasants," said one chronicler. He was wrong.

LEHKA_JIZDA.name: Light Cavalry
LEHKA_JIZDA.description: Fast cavalry for reconnaissance and flanking.

lore.description: Fast cavalry used for reconnaissance, flanking, and pursuit. Hungarian hussars and German reiters were feared opponents.
lore.equipment: Light lance, saber or sword, shield, leather or light mail armor
lore.origin: Hungary, Poland, German lands. Often hired mercenaries specialized in mounted combat.
lore.historicalNote: "Light cavalry is like a wolf - alone it cannot defeat a bear, but chases it to death."

ZVED_KRIZACI.name: Scout
ZVED_KRIZACI.description: Light horseman for reconnaissance. Sees 6 hexes, can quickly retreat.

lore.description: Scouts of the crusader army. Often local nobles or hired scouts who knew the terrain.
lore.equipment: Light armor, sword, possibly crossbow
lore.origin: Local nobility, mercenaries, sometimes even defectors
lore.historicalNote: "Finding Hussites isn't hard - follow the smoke of burning churches."

KOPINICI.name: Pikemen
KOPINICI.description: Infantry with long spears. Defensive hedgehog against cavalry.

lore.description: Disciplined infantry with long spears. They formed defensive lines protecting archers and artillery, or formed squares against cavalry.
lore.equipment: Long spear, short sword, helmet, gambeson or brigandine, sometimes pavise
lore.origin: Town militias from German imperial cities, mercenary companies
lore.historicalNote: "A German pikeman stands firm - until he hears howitzers."

HALAPARTNICI.name: Halberdiers
HALAPARTNICI.description: Infantry with halberds. Pulls riders from horses.

lore.description: Heavy infantry armed with halberds - combination of spear, axe, and hook. They could chop, stab, and pull riders from horses.
lore.equipment: Halberd (2-2.5 meters), short sword, helmet, mail armor or brigandine
lore.origin: Swiss mercenaries, German Landsknechts, town guards
lore.historicalNote: "The halberd is a weapon of clever men - it stabs, chops, and pulls down."

PAVEZNICI_KRIZACI.name: Pavise Bearers
PAVEZNICI_KRIZACI.description: Defenders with large shields. Protect archers.

lore.description: Defenders with large shields protecting archers. Crusader pavises were often richly decorated with coats of arms and religious symbols.
lore.equipment: Pavise (large, often painted with crosses), short sword, light armor
lore.origin: Town militias, specially trained mercenaries
lore.historicalNote: "Behind the pavise, a crossbowman is like behind a wall - until the wall moves."

lore.description: Elite mercenary archers from Italian Genoa, considered the best crossbowmen in Europe. Their crossbows had steel bows and great penetration.
lore.equipment: Heavy crossbow with steel bow, quiver with steel bolts, short sword, light armor, sometimes pavise
lore.origin: Republic of Genoa. Crossbowmen were an export article of Genoa and served throughout Europe.
lore.historicalNote: "A Genoese crossbow pierces armor like a knife through butter - at two hundred paces."

lore.description: Common crossbowmen forming ranged support for crusader armies. Less elite than Genoese, but still effective.
lore.equipment: Crossbow, quiver, short weapon, light armor
lore.origin: Town militias, mercenary companies
lore.historicalNote: "The crossbow is a coward's weapon, say the knights - but a dead knight says nothing."

LUCISTNICI.name: Archers
LUCISTNICI.description: Archers with longbows. Rapid fire (2 attacks/turn).

lore.description: Archers with bows, capable of faster shooting than crossbowmen, but with less penetration. Effective against unarmored infantry.
lore.equipment: Longbow or composite bow, quiver with arrows, short knife, minimal armor
lore.origin: English longbowmen, Hungarian horse archers, German huntsmen
lore.historicalNote: "An English archer shoots ten arrows while a crossbowman loads one - but only one in ten pierces armor."

lore.description: Massive siege gun capable of breaking down walls and wagon forts. Immobile on the battlefield, but devastating from a fixed position.
lore.equipment: Heavy bombard on wooden carriage, large stone or metal balls, crew of 8-12 men
lore.origin: Burgundian and German arsenals, Italian master gunners
lore.historicalNote: "The bombard breaks walls like the Lord broke the walls of Jericho - but more slowly."

lore.description: Heavy guns of crusader armies. Less mobile than Hussite ones, but equally devastating. Used mainly for sieges, but also in field battles.
lore.equipment: Heavy gun on carriage, gunpowder, stone/iron balls, crew of 6-8 men
lore.origin: Arsenals of imperial cities, Burgundian workshops, Italian gunners
lore.historicalNote: "The gun is king of the battlefield - a slow king, but his word is final."

lore.description: Professional warriors fighting for money. Experienced, tough, and reliable - as long as payment comes. They formed the backbone of many crusader armies.
lore.equipment: Various - swords, axes, spears, shields. Quality armor. Each had their preferred style.
lore.origin: Mercenary companies from all over Europe - Germans, Italians, Swiss, English
lore.historicalNote: "A mercenary doesn't ask who is right. He asks who has gold."

JAN_ZIZKA.name: Jan Žižka
JAN_ZIZKA.description: Legendary Hussite commander. Never lost a battle. Master of wagon tactics.

lore.description: Jan Žižka of Trocnov (c. 1360-1424) is the most famous Czech military commander of all time. He came from minor southern Bohemian nobility. As a mercenary, he fought in Poland against the Teutonic Order and possibly on the English side at Agincourt. After Jan Hus was burned at the stake, he became leader of the Hussite movement.
lore.equipment: Iron mace, short sword, light armor. After going blind, he wore a characteristic eye patch.
lore.origin: Trocnov near Borovany, southern Bohemia
lore.historicalNote: Žižka first went blind in one eye (before the Hussite Wars), then lost the other during the siege of Rábí castle in 1421. Nevertheless, he led armies for three more years and never lost a battle. He died of plague during the siege of Přibyslav. According to legend, he wished for his skin to be made into a drum, whose sound would terrify enemies even after his death.

PROKOP_HOLY.name: Prokop the Great
PROKOP_HOLY.description: Supreme Hetman of Tábor. Diplomat and unifier of Hussite factions.

lore.description: Prokop the Great, also called Prokop Holý (c. 1380-1434), was a priest and after Žižka's death the most important Hussite commander. He led the famous "Beautiful Rides" into Germany, Austria, and Hungary. Under his leadership, Hussites defeated the fourth and fifth crusades.
lore.equipment: Priestly habit under light armor, sword, prayer book.
lore.origin: Prague or surroundings
lore.historicalNote: Prokop the Great fell in the Battle of Lipany on May 30, 1434, where Hussites turned against each other. Moderate Utraquists defeated radical Taborites and Orphans. Lipany marked the end of Hussite military power.

JAN_ZELIVSKY.name: Jan Želivský
JAN_ZELIVSKY.description: Radical Prague preacher. Charismatic leader of the people, but no soldier.

lore.description: Jan Želivský (?-1422) was a radical Hussite priest and demagogue. On July 30, 1419, he led a procession to the New Town Hall, where the first Prague defenestration occurred. He became leader of Prague's poor and radicals, but was no soldier.
lore.equipment: Priestly habit, cross, bible.
lore.origin: Želiv (?)
lore.historicalNote: Želivský was executed on March 9, 1422, at Old Town Hall. Allegedly betrayed by moderate Prague citizens who feared his growing power. His death sparked popular unrest.

JAN_ROHAC.name: Jan Roháč of Dubá
JAN_ROHAC.description: Veteran of Hussite wars, Žižka's comrade-in-arms. Last unconquered Hussite commander.

lore.description: Jan Roháč of Dubá (c. 1400-1437) was a faithful lieutenant of Žižka and one of the most capable Hussite commanders. After Lipany, he refused to accept the Compactata and continued resistance from Sion castle near Kutná Hora.
lore.equipment: Full armor, sword, shield with Dubá family coat of arms.
lore.origin: Lords of Dubá family, eastern Bohemia
lore.historicalNote: Roháč was the last armed opponent of King Sigismund. After the fall of Sion, he was executed on September 9, 1437, with 52 companions in Prague's Old Town Square. He was the last victim of the Hussite Wars.

FRIDRICH_MISNENSKY.name: Frederick IV the Warlike
FRIDRICH_MISNENSKY.description: Margrave of Meissen. Promoted to Saxon Elector for victory at Most.

lore.description: Frederick IV the Warlike (1370-1428) was Margrave of Meissen and later Saxon Elector. One of the few commanders who achieved success against Hussites. In 1421, he defeated a Hussite detachment at Most.
lore.equipment: Full Gothic armor, sword, lance, banner with Saxon coat of arms.
lore.origin: House of Wettin, Meissen
lore.historicalNote: For his victory at Most, he received the Saxon Electorate from Sigismund in 1423. The Wettin family then held the title of Saxon Elector until 1918.

BOHUSLAV_SVAMBERK.name: Bohuslav of Švamberk
BOHUSLAV_SVAMBERK.description: Hetman of South Bohemian Landfrieden. Led Catholic lords against Žižka at Sudoměř.

lore.description: Bohuslav of Švamberk (?-1425) was a prominent South Bohemian Catholic nobleman and hetman of the royal Landfrieden. He led Catholic lords' army against Žižka in the Battle of Sudoměř on March 25, 1420.
lore.equipment: Full armor with Švamberk coat of arms (swan), lance, sword.
lore.origin: Lords of Švamberk family, western Bohemia
lore.historicalNote: At Sudoměř, he led 2,000 cavalry against 400 Hussites. Nevertheless, he suffered a crushing defeat. Žižka used narrow causeways between fishponds and cavalry could not deploy. The Hussites captured him at Krasíkov castle in 1421 - he then converted to the Hussite cause and fell in 1425 as a Taborite captain.

ZIKMUND.name: Sigismund of Luxembourg
ZIKMUND.description: King of the Romans and later Emperor. Organizer of crusades against Hussites.

lore.description: Sigismund of Luxembourg (1368-1437) was King of Hungary and the Romans, later Holy Roman Emperor. Son of Charles IV and younger brother of Wenceslaus IV. Main opponent of Hussites, who organized five crusades against them.
lore.equipment: Ornate armor decorated with gold, ceremonial sword, imperial crown.
lore.origin: House of Luxembourg, Prague
lore.historicalNote: Sigismund is a controversial figure in Czech history. On one hand, he was responsible for burning Jan Hus at Constance (violating his own safe conduct), on the other hand, he was a capable diplomat. Finally, he was accepted as Czech king in 1436.

FILIPPO_SCOLARI.name: Filippo Scolari
FILIPPO_SCOLARI.description: Italian condottiero called Pipo Spano. Commander of Hungarian cavalry, experienced warlord.

lore.description: Filippo Scolari (1369-1426), called Pipo Spano or Pipo of Ozora, was a Florentine merchant and condottiero in service of Hungarian King Sigismund. He became one of his most capable commanders and administrator of Transylvanian gold mines.
lore.equipment: Italian armor, lance, sword, banner with Hungarian emblem.
lore.origin: Florence, Italy
lore.historicalNote: Pipo Spano led Hungarian forces during the campaign into Bohemia in 1420. He was an experienced warrior who fought against Turks and in Italian wars. However, his cavalry tactics failed against Hussite wagon forts.

HEINRICH_ISENBURG.name: Henry of Isenburg
HEINRICH_ISENBURG.description: Meissen knight and commander of Vítkov assault. Experienced warrior.

lore.description: Henry of Isenburg was a Meissen knight and one of the commanders of crusader forces during the siege of Prague in 1420. He led the fateful assault on Vítkov Hill on July 14, 1420.
lore.equipment: Full Gothic armor, lance, sword, coat of arms of Isenburg family.
lore.origin: Counts of Isenburg family, Meissen
lore.historicalNote: Henry of Isenburg led elite Meissen knights in the assault on Vítkov. Although crusaders initially broke through defenses, Žižka's counterattack swept them away. Many knights perished, including Henry, or were captured.

FRIDRICH_SASKY.name: Frederick the Belligerent
FRIDRICH_SASKY.description: Duke of Saxony called the Belligerent. Commander of crusade at Ústí nad Labem 1426.

lore.description: Frederick IV the Warlike (1370-1428) was Margrave of Meissen and from 1423 Elector of Saxony. In 1426, his Saxon army launched a great crusade that ended in catastrophic defeat at Ústí nad Labem.
lore.equipment: Ornate Gothic armor, lance, sword, banner with Saxon coat of arms.
lore.origin: House of Wettin, Saxony
lore.historicalNote: The Battle of Ústí nad Labem (June 16, 1426) was one of the greatest defeats of crusaders. Against 70,000 crusaders stood only about 25,000 Hussites. Hussites killed or captured up to 15,000 enemies including many imperial princes.

PETR_STERNBERK.name: Peter of Šternberk
PETR_STERNBERK.description: Peter Konopišťský of Šternberk. Led assault on South Bohemian Hussite pilgrims at Živohošť.

lore.description: Peter Konopišťský of Šternberk (?-1420) was a Catholic nobleman and staunch opponent of Hussites. In November 1419, he led an attack on Hussite pilgrims at Živohošť. He fell a year later at the Battle of Vyšehrad.
lore.equipment: Full armor with Šternberk star, lance, sword.
lore.origin: Lords of Šternberk family, Konopiště
lore.historicalNote: At Živohošť, Peter of Šternberk attacked a group of Hussite pilgrims heading to Prague. Overwhelming numbers seemingly guaranteed success, but the arrival of Břeněk of Švihov with reinforcements changed the course of battle. Šternberk perished in the battle.

BRENEK_SVIHOVSKY.name: Břeněk of Švihov
BRENEK_SVIHOVSKY.description: Břeněk Švihovský of Rýzmburk. Brought 4,000 men from Nový Knín to aid at Živohošť.

lore.description: Břeněk Švihovský of Rýzmburk was a Hussite hetman operating in the Nový Knín area. His quick arrival with reinforcements decided the Battle of Živohošť in favor of Hussites.
lore.equipment: Armor, sword, shield with Švihov coat of arms.
lore.origin: Lords of Švihov family, western Bohemia
lore.historicalNote: At Živohošť, Břeněk brought about 4,000 men to aid Hussite pilgrims who were surrounded. His arrival changed the course of battle and Catholics suffered heavy defeat.

HYNEK_NEKMIRE.name: Hynek of Nekmíř
HYNEK_NEKMIRE.description: Hynek of Nekmíř, owner of Nekmíř fortress. Fell in battle against Žižka.

lore.description: Hynek of Nekmíř was a minor Catholic nobleman and owner of Nekmíř fortress in western Bohemia. He fell in one of the early battles against Žižka's Taborite army.
lore.equipment: Light armor, lance, sword.
lore.origin: Nekmíř fortress, Plzeň region
lore.historicalNote: Nekmíř was one of many minor nobles who opposed Hussites and paid with their lives. His fortress was captured and razed by Hussites.

HYNEK_KRUSINA.name: Hynek Krušina
HYNEK_KRUSINA.description: Hynek Krušina of Lichtenburg, 25-year-old Hussite commander at Vyšehrad. Decisive and brave.

lore.description: Hynek Krušina of Lichtenburg (c. 1395-1454) was a prominent Hussite hetman from powerful Lichtenburg family. As a young commander, he led Hussite army to victory at Vyšehrad in 1420.
lore.equipment: Full armor with Lichtenburg coat of arms, sword, shield.
lore.origin: Lords of Lichtenburg family, eastern Bohemia
lore.historicalNote: At Vyšehrad in 1420, Hynek Krušina led the decisive assault on royal forces. After the battle, he became one of the most prominent Hussite commanders. Later, he joined moderates and fought at Lipany against Taborites.

JINDRICH_PLUMOV.name: Henry of Plumlov
JINDRICH_PLUMOV.description: Henry of Plumlov, Moravian Land Hetman. Warned against Vyšehrad assault, accused of cowardice.

lore.description: Henry of Plumlov was Moravian Land Hetman and cautious commander. At Vyšehrad, he warned against hasty assault on Hussite positions, but his advice was not heeded.
lore.equipment: Armor with Moravian coat of arms, sword, lance.
lore.origin: Moravia
lore.historicalNote: At Vyšehrad, Henry of Plumlov correctly foresaw that direct assault on Hussite positions would fail. His warning was ignored and after defeat he was unjustly accused of cowardice, though his caution was justified.

DIVIS_BOREK.name: Diviš Bořek
DIVIS_BOREK.description: Diviš Bořek of Miletínek, hetman of Oreb Hussites. Žižka's comrade-in-arms at Hořice.

lore.description: Diviš Bořek of Miletínek (?-1438) was hetman of Oreb Hussites and faithful Žižka's comrade-in-arms. Orebites were a radical Hussite faction based in eastern Bohemia.
lore.equipment: Armor, sword, shield with Oreb chalice.
lore.origin: Miletínek, eastern Bohemia
lore.historicalNote: Diviš Bořek fought alongside Žižka in many battles including Hořice in 1423. After Žižka's death, Orebites renamed themselves Orphans in his honor. Diviš Bořek survived Lipany and died in 1438.

CENEK_VARTENBERK.name: Čeněk of Wartenberg
CENEK_VARTENBERK.description: Čeněk of Wartenberg, Supreme Burgrave of Prague. Leader of Catholic nobility at Hořice 1423.

lore.description: Čeněk of Wartenberg (c. 1380-1425) was Supreme Burgrave of Prague and one of the most influential figures at the start of Hussite Wars. Initially sympathetic to Hussites, but after radicalization of the movement joined Catholics.
lore.equipment: Ornate armor with Wartenberg coat of arms, sword, banner.
lore.origin: Lords of Wartenberg family, northern Bohemia
lore.historicalNote: Čeněk of Wartenberg changed sides several times. In 1419, he helped Hussites occupy Prague Castle, but later turned against them. At Hořice in 1423, he led Catholic nobility against Žižka and suffered defeat.

ARNOST_FLASKA.name: Arnošt Flaška
ARNOST_FLASKA.description: Arnošt Flaška of Pardubice, Catholic nobleman. Fell in Battle of Hořice 1423.

lore.description: Arnošt Flaška of Pardubice was a Catholic nobleman and distant relative of famous Archbishop Arnošt of Pardubice. He fought against Hussites in eastern Bohemia.
lore.equipment: Full armor with Pardubice coat of arms, lance, sword.
lore.origin: Flaška of Pardubice family, eastern Bohemia
lore.historicalNote: Arnošt Flaška fell in the Battle of Hořice on April 20, 1423. He was one of many Catholic nobles who paid with their lives for resistance against Žižka.

JINDRICH_BERKA.name: Henry Berka of Dubá
JINDRICH_BERKA.description: Henry Berka of Dubá, North Bohemian nobleman. Commander at Hořice 1423.

lore.description: Henry Berka of Dubá was a North Bohemian nobleman from powerful Berka of Dubá family. The family owned extensive estates in northern Bohemia including Houska castle.
lore.equipment: Armor with Berka coat of arms, lance, sword.
lore.origin: Berka of Dubá family, northern Bohemia
lore.historicalNote: The Berka of Dubá family was one of the oldest and most powerful Czech noble families. Henry participated in the Battle of Hořice on the side of Catholic coalition led by Čeněk of Wartenberg.

JAN_HVEZDA.name: Jan Hvězda of Vícemilice
JAN_HVEZDA.description: Jan Hvězda of Vícemilice, called Bzdinka. Expert on Malešov area, Žižka's guide.

lore.description: Jan Hvězda of Vícemilice, nicknamed Bzdinka, was a Hussite hetman and expert on the area around Kutná Hora and Malešov. He served as guide to blind Žižka.
lore.equipment: Light armor, sword, shield.
lore.origin: Vícemilice, central Bohemia
lore.historicalNote: Jan Hvězda helped blind Žižka orient himself in the terrain at Malešov. His knowledge of local terrain was crucial for success of Hussite tactics in the battle on June 7, 1424.

HYNEK_PODEBRADY.name: Hynek of Poděbrady
HYNEK_PODEBRADY.description: Hynek of Poděbrady and Kunštát, Oreb ally. Father of future King George of Poděbrady.

lore.description: Hynek of Poděbrady and Kunštát (?-1426) was a Moravian nobleman and Hussite ally. He was the uncle of George of Poděbrady, future Czech king - George's father was Hynek's brother Viktorin Boček of Kunštát.
lore.equipment: Armor with Kunštát coat of arms, sword, shield.
lore.origin: Poděbrady and Kunštát, eastern Bohemia and Moravia
lore.historicalNote: Hynek of Poděbrady fought on the side of Orebites at Malešov in 1424. His son George was born in 1420 and became Czech king in 1458 - the only Hussite on Czech throne.

VIKTORIN_BOCEK.name: Viktorín Boček
VIKTORIN_BOCEK.description: Viktorín Boček of Poděbrady, brother of Hynek. Valiant commander of Hussite cavalry.

lore.description: Viktorín Boček of Poděbrady was brother of Hynek of Poděbrady and uncle of future King George. He excelled as cavalry commander in Hussite ranks.
lore.equipment: Armor, lance, sword, shield with Kunštát coat of arms.
lore.origin: Poděbrady, eastern Bohemia
lore.historicalNote: Viktorín Boček fought alongside his brother Hynek at Malešov in 1424. The Poděbrady family belonged to moderate Hussite wing and after wars became one of the most powerful in Bohemia.

VOZOVA_HRADBA_PRASKY.name: Prague Wagons
VOZOVA_HRADBA_PRASKY.description: Wagon fort of moderate Utraquists from Prague.

lore.description: War wagons of moderate Utraquists from Prague. Used in civil war between Hussites at Lipany.
lore.equipment: Reinforced wagons with chains, crew of defenders and shooters
lore.origin: Prague and surroundings
lore.historicalNote: At Lipany, Prague Utraquists fought against radical Taborites using same tactics that made Hussites famous.

lore.description: Flailmen of moderate Utraquists from Prague. Even in civil war, they wielded flails with same ferocity.
lore.equipment: War flails, light armor, helmets
lore.origin: Prague
lore.historicalNote: Prague flailmen fought at Lipany against their former radical comrades.

lore.description: Crossbowmen of moderate Utraquists. Their crossbows were just as deadly against former allies.
lore.equipment: Crossbows, light armor
lore.origin: Prague
lore.historicalNote: Hussite crossbowmen turned their weapons against radical Hussites at Lipany.

lore.description: Howitzers of moderate Utraquists. Ironic that Hussite invention was used against radical Hussites.
lore.equipment: Field howitzers, gunpowder, iron balls
lore.origin: Prague foundries
lore.historicalNote: At Lipany, Prague artillery bombarded Taborite positions.

lore.description: Cavalry of moderate Utraquists from Prague. Mostly gentry and wealthy townsmen.
lore.equipment: Light armor, lances, swords
lore.origin: Prague and surroundings
lore.historicalNote: Prague cavalry fought against Taborites at Lipany, ending radical phase of Hussite revolution.

tutorial.name: Training at Tábor
tutorial.description: Learn combat basics in interactive training.
tutorial.historicalSignificance: Before the first battles, every warrior must undergo training.

briefing.hussites: Welcome, recruit! I'm Jan Žižka and I'll teach you how to fight for the chalice. Follow my instructions carefully.

steps.title: Welcome, warrior!
steps.text: I'm Jan Žižka. I'll teach you combat basics. Click on a unit to select it, green fields show where it can move.

steps.title: Unit selected!
steps.text: Green fields = possible movement. Red fields = possible attack. Click where you want to go or who to attack.

steps.title: Movement complete!
steps.text: Each unit can perform MOVEMENT and ATTACK per turn. When done, click 'End Turn' or press ENTER.

steps.title: End of turn
steps.text: Now the enemy plays. After their turn, it's your turn again. Destroy all enemies for victory!

steps.title: Attack!
steps.text: In melee both sides take damage (counterattack). Shooters attack at range WITHOUT counterattack.

steps.title: Tip: Terrain
steps.text: Hills give +20% defense, forests +15%. Use terrain! Units near wagon fort also get bonus.

steps.title: Defensive stance
steps.text: Now learn DEFENSIVE STANCE. Select unit and press D key or click 'Defend'. Unit gains +30% defense.

steps.title: Defensive stance activated!
steps.text: Defending unit has +30% defense, but can't attack. Excellent for holding position. Now destroy all enemies!

steps.title: Training complete!
steps.text: You learned basics: selection, movement, attack, defense and terrain. You're ready for real battle! Good luck.

debriefing.victory: Training successfully completed! You're ready to fight for the chalice.
debriefing.defeat: No worries, try again. Even Žižka had to learn.

phases.name: Training
phases.description: Interactive training in combat basics.

zivohost_1419.name: Battle of Živohošť
zivohost_1419.description: First major clash of the Hussite Wars. South Bohemian pilgrims must survive the attack until reinforcements arrive.
zivohost_1419.historicalSignificance: Demonstration of necessity for organized defense, precursor to wagon fort.

briefing.hussites: Your small group of South Bohemian pilgrims has been surprised at Živohošť. Retreat to Červenka hill and build improvised defenses. Reinforcements from Nový Knín are on their way!
briefing.crusaders: Catch up with the Hussite pilgrims before they get help. You have the advantage - use it!

reinforcements.hussites: Reinforcements from Nový Knín arrive! Břeněk Švihovský leads detachment to help!

events.message: Petr ze Šternberka caught up with you! Fortify on Červenka hill!

events.text: TIP: Your units are close to hill. Move them to green fields for defensive bonus.
TIP: Wagon provides protection to surrounding units. Shooters from hill get attack bonus.

events.message: Břeněk Švihovský brings reinforcements! Hold positions!
Šternberk sees superiority and hesitates. Now is the time to strike!

objectives.primary: Survive until reinforcements arrive (turn 5) with at least 40% units
secondary: Capture or kill Petr ze Šternberka

debriefing.victory: Reinforcements from Nový Knín arrived in time! Petr ze Šternberka retreated when he saw determined defense on the hill. Improvised wagon as seed of future wagon fort showed the way to new method of warfare.
debriefing.defeat: South Bohemian pilgrims were scattered. Petr ze Šternberka celebrates victory. Hussite movement suffered heavy blow right at the beginning.

phases.name: Surprise Attack
phases.description: Šternberk attacks tired South Bohemian pilgrims.

events.message: Petr ze Šternberka caught up with you! Fortify on Červenka hill!

events.text: TIP: Your units are close to hill. Move them to green fields for defensive bonus.

phases.name: Defense on the Hill
phases.description: Hussites build improvised defenses.

events.text: TIP: Wagon provides protection to surrounding units. Shooters from hill get attack bonus.

phases.name: Reinforcements Arrive
phases.description: Reinforcements from Nový Knín come to help.

events.message: Břeněk Švihovský brings reinforcements! Hold positions!

phases.name: Counterattack
phases.description: With reinforcements you can counterattack.

events.message: Šternberk sees superiority and hesitates. Now is the time to strike!

nekmir_1419.name: Battle of Nekmíř
nekmir_1419.description: FIRST DOCUMENTED USE OF WAGON FORT! Jan Žižka with small group repels attack by Plzeň landfrieden.
nekmir_1419.historicalSignificance: Historically first known use of wagon fort. Birth of tactic that will change warfare.

briefing.hussites: You're heading from Plzeň toward enemy fortress Nekmíř. Plzeň landfrieden caught up with you! You only have 7 wagons - not enough for closed circle. Form semicircle and defend!
briefing.crusaders: Catch up with Hussite heretics before they destroy Nekmíř fortress. You have clear numerical superiority. Destroy them!

events.message: Plzeň landfrieden caught up with Hussite column! Quickly form wagon fort!

events.text: TIP: You only have 7 wagons - not enough for closed circle. Form semicircle open toward fortress.

events.message: Žižka: 'Pull wagons together! Shooters behind wagons, flailmen ready!'

events.text: Wagon fort is ready! +3 to defense for units behind wagons.

events.message: Landfrieden heavy cavalry attacks! Will wagon fort hold?

events.text: Cavalry hit wagons! Charge bonus negated!

events.message: (Historically at this stage Hynek of Nekmíř fell - fortress owner)
Cavalry repelled! Landfrieden withdraws!
Victory! Žižka proved wagon fort works!

objectives.primary: Repel landfrieden attack and survive until turn 10 with 50% units

debriefing.victory: First wagon fort in history held! Žižka proved even small group with wagons can withstand superior numbers. Plzeň landfrieden was driven away and Nekmíř fortress captured. Tactic was born that will change European warfare.
debriefing.defeat: Improvised wagon fort didn't withstand enemy pressure. Hussite raid ended in disaster. However Žižka survived and learned - next time fort will be stronger and closed.

phases.name: Hussite Sortie from Plzeň
phases.description: Žižka marches from Plzeň towards Nekmíř.

events.message: Plzeň landfrieden caught up with Hussite column! Quickly form wagon fort!

events.text: TIP: You only have 7 wagons - not enough for closed circle. Form semicircle open toward fortress.

phases.name: Formation of First Wagon Fort
phases.description: Žižka orders new defensive formation.

events.message: Žižka: "Pull wagons together! Shooters behind wagons, flailmen ready!"

events.text: Wagon fort is ready! +3 to defense for units behind wagons.

phases.name: Cavalry Attack on Wagon Fort
phases.description: Švamberk throws cavalry against wagons.

events.message: Heavy cavalry of landfrieden attacks! Will wagon fort hold?

events.text: Cavalry hit the wagons! Charge bonus negated!

phases.name: Key Phase of Battle
phases.description: Decisive moment of clash.

events.message: (Historically at this phase Hynek of Nekmíř - fortress owner - fell)

phases.name: Landfrieden Retreat
phases.description: Catholics retreat, Hussites continue to fortress.

events.message: Cavalry is repelled! Landfrieden withdraws!
Victory! Žižka proved wagon fort works!

sudomere_1420.name: Battle of Sudoměř
sudomere_1420.description: First major Hussite victory. Jan Žižka with small army defends dam between fishponds against superior Catholic lords.
sudomere_1420.historicalSignificance: First successful use of wagon fort in battle.

briefing.hussites: Your small group of pilgrims is pursued by army of Catholic lords. Use dam between fishponds and build wagon fort. You must survive until nightfall.
briefing.crusaders: Catch up and destroy Hussite heretics before they fortify. Attack quickly, before fog falls.

events.message: Crusaders begin attack along narrow dam!
Thick fog falling! Visibility drops.

objectives.primary: Survive until turn 12 with at least 50% units

debriefing.victory: Fishpond and swamps became grave for iron lords! Hussites used terrain and repelled superior numbers. This battle showed that properly chosen battlefield can balance even significant numerical disadvantage. Žižka's genius fully manifested.
debriefing.defeat: Swamps of Sudoměř became trap not for enemy, but for you. Knights broke through your defense. Žižka's career ends before it could truly begin.

phases.name: Initial Deployment
phases.description: Hussites fortify on dyke, Catholics approach.

phases.name: Frontal Attack
phases.description: Knights Hospitaller and royal army attack along dyke.

events.message: Crusaders begin attack along narrow dam!

phases.name: Fog and Confusion
phases.description: Fog descends, Catholics lose orientation.

events.message: Thick fog falling! Visibility drops.

vitkov_1420.name: Battle of Vítkov
vitkov_1420.description: Defense of Prague against first crusade. Small garrison on Vítkov must hold until reinforcements arrive.
vitkov_1420.historicalSignificance: Turning point of first crusade, defense of Prague.

briefing.hussites: You defend wooden fortifications on Vítkov with handful of men and women. Crusaders attack in superior numbers. Hold until reinforcements from Prague arrive!
briefing.crusaders: Capture Hussite fortifications on Vítkov and open way to Prague.

reinforcements.hussites: Jan Žižka leads reinforcements from Prague!

objectives.primary: Survive until turn 8 with at least 30% units

debriefing.victory: Vítkov held! Žižka with handful of defenders, including women, repelled thousands of crusaders. Sigismund lost hope of quick conquest of Prague. This victory encouraged Hussite movement and showed that determined defenders can defeat even superior numbers.
debriefing.defeat: Fortifications on Vítkov fell and with them Prague's hope. Crusaders occupied strategic height and Prague is under siege. Hussite revolution ends before it could develop its strength.

phases.name: Attack on the neck
phases.description: Meissen and Austrian cavalry attack through the forest.

phases.name: Fight for the fortifications
phases.description: Crusaders penetrate to the fortifications. Reinforcements from Prague are on the way!

phases.name: Counterattack
phases.description: Hussites push crusaders off the hill.

vysehrad_1420.name: Battle under Vyšehrad
vysehrad_1420.description: Decisive Hussite victory. Sigismund arrives late and Czech nobility is slaughtered in ravine below Podolí.
vysehrad_1420.historicalSignificance: Prague fully in Hussite hands. Loss of Czech nobility's trust in Sigismund. 25 banner lords fell.

briefing.hussites: You've been besieging Vyšehrad since September. Garrison negotiated capitulation for 8:00 - if Sigismund doesn't come earlier. It's All Saints' Day and royal army approaches. Defend your positions!
briefing.crusaders: You must break through to Vyšehrad and save garrison! Czech nobility attacks from Podolí, main force frontally.

events.message: It's after 15:00. Vyšehrad garrison already capitulated - can't help you!
Sigismund vainly waves sword toward Vyšehrad. It's too late.
Hungarians and Germans begin frontal attack on your trenches!

events.text: Prepared positions provide +3 to defense!

events.message: Jindřich of Plumlov warns against attack through slope. Sigismund accuses him of cowardice!
Insulted Czech nobility attacks! Must dismount due to steep slope.

events.text: Czech nobility loses cavalry advantage on steep slope!

events.message: Hynek Krušina deploys Orebite flailmen from reserve!

events.text: Units freed from Vyšehrad siege join battle!

events.message: Czech nobility trapped in ravine! Can't escape!

events.text: Taborites and Orebites took no prisoners... Massacre in ravine!

events.message: Sigismund orders retreat! Royal army flees toward Český Brod.
Victory! Prague fully in Hussite hands. 25 banner lords fell.

objectives.primary: Defend St. Pankrác church until turn 15

debriefing.victory: Decisive victory under Vyšehrad! 25 banner lords of Czech nobility fell in ravine below Podolí. Vyšehrad garrison capitulated and Prague is fully in Hussite hands. Sigismund came late and with him Czech nobility's trust in his abilities.
debriefing.defeat: Sigismund's forces broke through to Vyšehrad in time. Garrison was saved and Hussites suffered heavy losses. Siege of Prague continues and Hussite cause is endangered.

phases.name: Sigismund arrives late
phases.description: Royal army arrives after 15:00 - hour after the ultimatum.

events.message: It's after 15:00. Vyšehrad garrison already capitulated - can't help you!
Sigismund vainly waves sword toward Vyšehrad. It's too late.

phases.name: Attack on Pankrác fortifications
phases.description: Hungarians and Germans attack Hussite trenches frontally.

events.message: Hungarians and Germans begin frontal attack on your trenches!

events.text: Prepared positions provide +3 to defense!

phases.name: Flank attack by Czech nobility
phases.description: Czech and Moravian nobility attack from Podolí.

events.message: Jindřich of Plumlov warns against attack through slope. Sigismund accuses him of cowardice!
Insulted Czech nobility attacks! Must dismount due to steep slope.

events.text: Czech nobility loses cavalry advantage on steep slope!

phases.name: Hussite counterattack
phases.description: Hynek Krušina deploys reserves.

events.message: Hynek Krušina deploys Oreb flailmen from reserve!

events.text: Units freed from besieging Vyšehrad join the battle!

phases.name: Massacre of Czech nobility
phases.description: Nobility trapped in ravine and slaughtered.

events.message: Czech nobility stuck in ravine! Cannot escape!

events.text: Taborites and Orebites took no prisoners... Massacre in the ravine!

phases.name: General retreat
phases.description: Sigismund orders retreat.

events.message: Sigismund orders retreat! Royal army flees to Český Brod.
Victory! Prague is fully in Hussite hands. 25 banner lords fell.

kutna_hora_1421.name: Battle of Kutná Hora
kutna_hora_1421.description: Žižka surrounded by superior forces at Kutná Hora after townsmen's betrayal. Must break through with wagon fort at night!
kutna_hora_1421.historicalSignificance: First offensive use of firearms from moving wagon fort. Brilliant tactical retreat.

briefing.hussites: Kutná Hora miners betrayed you and let crusaders into city! You're encircled. Prepare night breakthrough with wagon fort - must break toward Kolín to southwest!
briefing.crusaders: Hussites are trapped! We've surrounded them before city. Destroy Žižka's wagon fort before he escapes!

events.message: Kutná Hora miners opened Kolín Gate! Crusaders pour into city - you're surrounded!
Žižka prepares night breakthrough. Form wagon fort heading southwest!
BREAKTHROUGH! Fire from wagons while moving! Handgunners - fire into darkness!
Crusaders in night chaos can't coordinate defense!
You broke through encirclement! Retreat southwest toward Kolín!
You're safe! Crusaders can't stop you. Žižka already planning counterattack...

objectives.primary: Get at least 5 units to southwest edge of map (toward Kolín)

debriefing.victory: Brilliant night breakthrough! Žižka led entire wagon fort out of encirclement under fire from own hand cannons. This is first documented use of firearms from moving wagons. Kutná Hora traitors will be punished, but Žižka's army escaped to safety.
debriefing.defeat: Breakthrough failed. Wagon fort was broken and Žižka's army destroyed. Kutná Hora remains in enemy hands and Hussite movement loses its most capable commander.

phases.name: Encirclement
phases.description: Kutná Hora people betrayed! Crusaders close in from all sides.

events.message: Kutná Hora miners opened Kolín Gate! Crusaders pour into city - you are encircled!
Žižka prepares night breakthrough. Form wagon fort toward southwest!

phases.name: Night breakthrough
phases.description: At five in the morning Žižka begins breakthrough! Firearms shoot from moving wagons.

events.message: BREAKTHROUGH! Fire from wagons while moving! Handgunners - fire into darkness!
Crusaders in night confusion cannot coordinate defense!

phases.name: Retreat to Kaňk
phases.description: Hussites broke through! Retreat to Kolín under wagon fort protection.

events.message: You broke through encirclement! Retreat southwest to Kolín!
You are safe! Crusaders cannot stop you. Žižka is already planning counterattack...

nemecky_brod_1422.name: Battle of Německý Brod
nemecky_brod_1422.description: Pursuit of retreating Sigismund's army from Kutná Hora. Ice on Sázava breaks under heavy wagons.
nemecky_brod_1422.historicalSignificance: End of 2nd crusade. Sigismund's last campaign in Bohemia. Loot of 500 wagons.

briefing.hussites: Sigismund flees from Kutná Hora toward Německý Brod! Pursue retreating army and destroy it before it escapes across Sázava. Careful - ice on river is thin!
briefing.crusaders: Retreat! Must get across Sázava to Německý Brod. Bridge is overcrowded - part of army must cross frozen river.

events.message: Sigismund fled! Scolari's army retreats toward Německý Brod. Pursue them!
Crusaders abandon loot along way. Don't get distracted - destroy army!
Scolari's rearguard tries to stop advance on hill at Habry!
Crusaders can't hold positions - begin fleeing toward river!
Bridge is overcrowded! Part of army tries to cross frozen Sázava!
Ice cracks under heavy wagons! River swallows fleeing!
Royal army scattered! Collect loot and finish off remnants of resistance.
Victory! 500 wagons of loot captured. Second crusade ended.

objectives.primary: Destroy at least 70% of royal army

debriefing.victory: Catastrophe of crusader army! Sigismund's men fled across frozen Sázava and ice broke beneath them. Dozens of knights drowned in their armor. 500 wagons of provisions fell into your hands. 2nd crusade ends in complete debacle.
debriefing.defeat: Sigismund escaped! Most of his army crossed Sázava and burned bridge behind them. Loot is minimal and next crusade will come much sooner.

phases.name: Pursuit from Kutná Hora
phases.description: Žižka's army pursues retreating crusaders.

events.message: Sigismund fled! Scolari's army retreating to Německý Brod. Pursue them!
Crusaders leave loot along the way. Don't get distracted - destroy the army!

phases.name: Clash at Habry
phases.description: Crusaders try to stop Hussites on hill at Habry.

events.message: Scolari's rearguard tries to stop advance on hill at Habry!
Crusaders cannot hold positions - begin fleeing to river!

phases.name: Flight across Sázava
phases.description: Panicking army rushes to bridge and onto frozen river.

events.message: Bridge is overcrowded! Part of army tries to cross frozen Sázava!
Ice cracks under heavy wagons! River swallows the fleeing!

phases.name: Destruction of retreating army
phases.description: Hussites finish off remnants of royal army.

events.message: Royal army is scattered! Collect loot and finish off resistance.
Victory! 500 wagons of loot captured. Second crusade ended.

most_1421.name: Battle of Most
most_1421.description: Želivský's unsuccessful siege of Hněvín castle. Praguers besiege, but help comes from south.
most_1421.historicalSignificance: First major Hussite defeat. Showed that without Žižka and without wagon fort Hussites lose.

briefing.hussites: Hněvín castle is almost ours! Garrison offered capitulation, but Želivský refused. You have two goals: capture castle OR block city gate from which reinforcements may come. You don't have enough men for both - decide!
briefing.crusaders: Hold castle at all costs! Margrave Frederick's reinforcements are on way. Most townsmen will sally from gate and strike Hussites in flank.

events.message: Želivský: 'No mercy for traitors! We'll take castle by force!'
Castle garrison defends stubbornly. Noise comes from city...
Most townsmen sally from city gate! Flank attack!
You must decide - continue attack on castle, or turn around?
Meissen banners on horizon! Margrave Frederick comes with reinforcements!
Attack on castle now very risky. Consider alternative goal.
Time running out! Hold gate, or capture castle!
Last chance! Either fulfill goal, or all is lost.

objectives.primary: Fulfill ONE goal: Capture Hněvín castle OR keep city gate blocked

debriefing.victory: Hněvín castle is yours! Combination of castle capture and city gate blocking paid off. Most is under Hussite control and way to Saxony is open for future Beautiful Rides.
debriefing.defeat: Most townsmen and castle garrison held their positions. Hussite attack failed and army must retreat. Northwestern Bohemia remains in enemy hands.

phases.name: Siege
phases.description: Hněvín castle is within reach. Garrison offered capitulation, but Želivský refused.

events.message: Želivský: "No mercy for traitors! We shall take castle by force!"
Castle garrison defends stubbornly. Noise comes from city...

phases.name: Flank strike
phases.description: Most townsmen sallied from gate! Strike to flank of Hussite army.

events.message: Most militia sallies from city gate! Flank strike!
You must decide - continue castle assault, or turn around?

phases.name: Arrival of reinforcements
phases.description: Meissen army! Margrave Friedrich comes from north!

events.message: Meissen banners on horizon! Margrave Friedrich comes with reinforcements!
Castle assault is now very risky. Consider alternative objective.

phases.name: Decision
phases.description: Complete at least one objective, or face defeat.

events.message: Time is running out! Hold the gate, or take the castle!
Last chance! Either complete objective, or all is lost.

usti_1426.name: Battle of Ústí nad Labem
usti_1426.description: Bloodiest defeat of crusaders. Hussites with double wagon fort decimate attacking Saxons.
usti_1426.historicalSignificance: Last major frontal attack on wagon fort. Crusader losses: 4,000, Hussite: 30.

briefing.hussites: Build double wagon fort on Na Běhání hill. Let enemy come to you and destroy them with fire.
briefing.crusaders: Break through Hussite fortifications and liberate besieged Ústí nad Labem.

events.message: Saxon army begins attack in unbearable heat!
'They're running! Germans running!' - crusaders flee!

objectives.primary: Hold wagon fort and destroy 50% of crusaders

debriefing.victory: Massacre at Na Běhání! 4,000 crusaders fell, while Hussites lost only 30 men. Double wagon fort proved insurmountable obstacle. Saxon duchy is decimated and will never send army against Hussites again.
debriefing.defeat: Saxon cavalry broke through your fort! Catastrophic Hussite defeat changes balance of power. Without wagon fort you're defenseless against heavy cavalry.

phases.name: Crusader attack
phases.description: Germans attack in scorching heat.

events.message: Saxon army begins attack in unbearable heat!

phases.name: Fire from wagons
phases.description: Hussite firearms decimate attackers.

phases.name: Panic and flight
phases.description: Crusaders break into headlong flight.

events.message: "They run! Germans run!" - crusaders flee!

tachov_1427.name: Battle of Tachov
tachov_1427.description: Fourth crusade ends in flight. Crusaders flee before Hussites without daring to fight.
tachov_1427.historicalSignificance: Psychological victory of Hussites - their reputation alone suffices to defeat crusaders. Cardinal Beaufort tears imperial banners.

briefing.hussites: Crusaders unsuccessfully besieged Stříbro and now withdraw toward Tachov. Approach quickly and exploit their demoralization. Pursue fleeing and capture Tachov!
briefing.crusaders: Hussites approach! Your army is demoralized after unsuccessful siege of Stříbro. Try to organize defense, or retreat to Bavarian borders.

events.message: Hussite army approaches from Stříbro! 16,000 infantry and 1,500 cavalry under Prokop the Great.

events.text: Jindřich of Plaveň's cavalry returns without fight - refused to attack Hussites!
Entire crusader detachments abandon camp and flee toward borders!

events.message: Cardinal Beaufort vainly tries to stop fleeing soldiers.

events.text: Beaufort in anger tears imperial banners and throws them at princes' feet!
Remnants of crusader army take flight toward Bavarian borders!

events.message: Hussites find abandoned crusader camp full of supplies and weapons.

objectives.primary: Destroy or rout 50% of crusader army
secondary: Destroy 75% of enemies before their escape

debriefing.victory: Fourth crusade ends in complete debacle! Crusaders fled without daring to fight. Cardinal Beaufort in desperation tore imperial banners. Few days later Hussites capture Tachov - August 11 city and August 14 castle. Prokop the Great becomes most powerful man in Bohemia.
debriefing.defeat: Crusaders managed to overcome fear and organize defense. Hussite reputation of invincibility got crack. Tachov remains in enemy hands.

phases.name: Hussite march
phases.description: Hussites advance from Stříbro. Crusaders send cavalry to slow advance.

events.message: Hussite army approaches from Stříbro! 16,000 infantry and 1,500 cavalry under Prokop the Great.

events.text: Jindřich of Plavno's cavalry returns without fight - refused to attack Hussites!

phases.name: Panic in camp
phases.description: Fear spreads through crusader camp. Units begin deserting.

events.text: Entire crusader units abandon camp and flee to borders!

events.message: Cardinal Beaufort vainly tries to stop fleeing soldiers.

events.text: Beaufort in rage tears imperial banners and throws them at princes' feet!

phases.name: Flight to Bavaria
phases.description: Crusader army flees. Hussites pursue and capture abandoned camp.

events.text: Remnants of crusader army flee to Bavarian borders!

events.message: Hussites find abandoned crusader camp full of supplies and weapons.

nisa_1428.name: Battle of Nysa
nisa_1428.description: Beautiful Ride into Silesia. Hussites crushingly defeat Silesian army before Nysa walls.
nisa_1428.historicalSignificance: Only major battle of Silesian raid. After this victory cities surrendered without fight or paid tribute.

briefing.hussites: After successful raid into Hungary we continue to Silesia. Before Nysa walls awaits us army of Wrocław bishop. Crush them and burn suburbs!
briefing.crusaders: Hussites march on Nysa! Gather peasants and townsmen for defense. City must be defended at all costs!

events.message: Hussite army advances with wagons and guns against Nysa defenders!
Peasants and villagers resist Hussites before suburbs.

events.text: Silesian detachments begin retreating under pressure of Hussite attack!

events.message: Půta of Častolovic tries to organize defense at walls.

events.text: Defenders flee in panic - many die in river Nysa!

events.message: Hussites burn suburbs and attack walls!

debriefing.victory: Crushing victory! Silesian army scattered, about two thousand defenders fell or drowned in river Nysa. Suburbs in flames. Půta of Častolovic held city, but no Silesian city dares oppose Hussites anymore. Beautiful Ride continues - cities surrender or pay tribute.
debriefing.defeat: Silesian defense held. Půta of Častolovic successfully defended Nysa. Beautiful Ride must continue elsewhere and Hussite reputation of invincibility suffered crack.

phases.name: Hussite attack
phases.description: Hussites begin attack on Silesian army before walls.

events.message: Hussite army advances with wagons and guns against Nysa defenders!
Peasants and villagers oppose Hussites before suburbs.

phases.name: Breakthrough of defense
phases.description: Hussites break through Silesian defense.

events.text: Silesian units begin retreating under pressure of Hussite attack!

events.message: Půta of Častolovic tries to organize defense at walls.

phases.name: Massacre and flight
phases.description: Defenders flee, many perish in river.

events.text: Defenders flee in panic - many perish in river Nysa!

events.message: Hussites burn suburbs and attack walls!

domazlice_1431.name: Battle of Domažlice
domazlice_1431.description: Greatest Hussite victory. Mere sound of Hussite choral causes crusader army flight.
domazlice_1431.historicalSignificance: Crusaders flee upon hearing 'Ktož jsú boží bojovníci'. End of fourth crusade.

briefing.hussites: You approach Domažlice at fast march. Crusaders panic - sing choral and pursue fleeing!
briefing.crusaders: Hussites approach! Try to form defense, or at least safely retreat to Bavaria.

events.message: Hussite army covered 80 km in 2 days and approaches Domažlice!

events.text: Scouts report: Hussites closer than we expected!
Sound of choral terrifies crusaders!
Crusaders hear Hussite choral and fall to fear!

events.message: Cardinal Cesarini flees and loses cardinal hat!

events.text: Panic spreads through crusader camp!
Entire crusader army takes flight!

debriefing.victory: Glorious victory! Mere sound of 'Ktož jsú boží bojovníci' caused panic flight of crusader army. 5th crusade ends in absolute debacle - crusaders flee without attempting fight. This is peak of Hussite glory!
debriefing.defeat: Crusaders overcame their fear and formed defense. Despite your choral they didn't collapse. Hussite reputation of invincibility is shaken.

phases.name: Hussite march
phases.description: Hussites rapidly approach Domažlice.

events.message: Hussite army covered 80 km in 2 days and approaches Domažlice!

events.text: Scouts report: Hussites are closer than we expected!

phases.name: Choral and panic
phases.description: Crusaders hear 'Ktož jsú boží bojovníci' and panic.

events.text: Sound of choral terrifies crusaders!
Crusaders hear Hussite choral and fall into fear!

events.message: Cardinal Cesarini flees and loses cardinal hat!

events.text: Panic spreads through crusader camp!

phases.name: Flight to Bavaria
phases.description: Crusaders flee through Všeruby pass to Bavaria.

events.text: Entire crusader army breaks into flight!

oblehani_plzne_1433.name: Siege of Plzeň
oblehani_plzne_1433.description: General assault on Catholic Plzeň. Nine months of siege culminates in attempt to breach walls.
oblehani_plzne_1433.historicalSignificance: Greatest Hussite failure. Plzeň resisted almost year and received camel in coat of arms.

briefing.hussites: After months of siege time for decisive assault! Break through walls and capture city. Prokop the Great watches from rear - mustn't fail!
briefing.crusaders: Hussites prepare general assault! Vilém Švihovský of Rýzmburk leads defense. Hold walls at all costs!

events.message: Hussite bombards begin firing on Plzeň walls!
Defenders shelter behind battlements. Vilém Švihovský encourages garrison.
First cracks appear in walls!
Jan Pardus of Horka leads Taborite infantry into assault!
Defenders pour hot pitch and stones on attackers.
Bloody fights at walls! Hussites try to break through defense.
Vilém Švihovský leads sally from gates! Attackers surprised!

events.text: Defenders' morale grows! Captured Hussite camel!

events.message: Last chance for breakthrough! Prokop the Great sends reserves.
Hussite losses too high. Some soldiers desert.

objectives.primary: Occupy at least 3 positions inside city walls

debriefing.victory: Incredible success! Plzeň walls fell after nine months of siege. Prokop the Great triumphs and Catholic bastion in western Bohemia is captured. History changes - without Plzeň moderates lose key ally and radicals strengthen their power.
debriefing.defeat: Plzeň held! Despite months of siege and repeated assaults walls held. Hussites suffered heavy losses and must withdraw. This fiasco weakens Prokop the Great and strengthens his opponents. Plzeň will receive camel in coat of arms from Emperor Sigismund for its bravery.

phases.name: Artillery preparation
phases.description: Hussite guns bombard walls. Defenders respond from city positions.

events.message: Hussite bombards open fire on Plzeň walls!
Defenders take cover behind battlements. Vilém Švihovský encourages garrison.
First cracks appear in walls!

phases.name: Assault on walls
phases.description: Infantry advances to walls. Heavy losses on both sides.

events.message: Jan Pardus of Horka leads Taborite infantry to attack!
Defenders pour hot tar and stones on attackers.
Bloody fighting at walls! Hussites try to break defense.

phases.name: Defenders' sortie
phases.description: Plzeň people make daring sortie!

events.message: Vilém Švihovský leads sortie from gates! Attackers surprised!

events.text: Defenders' confidence grows! Captured Hussite camel!

phases.name: Decision
phases.description: Attack either succeeds, or Hussites must retreat.

events.message: Last chance for breakthrough! Prokop the Great sends reserves.
Hussite losses too high. Some soldiers desert.

lipany_1434.name: Battle of Lipany
lipany_1434.description: Fratricidal battle between Hussites. Moderate Utraquists and Catholics defeat radical Taborites and Orphans.
lipany_1434.historicalSignificance: End of Hussite Wars. Death of Prokop the Great. Victory of moderates.

briefing.hussites: As commander of radicals you must repel attack by moderates. Beware their trap - feigned retreat!
briefing.crusaders: You lead coalition of moderates. Use feigned retreat, lure radicals from wagon fort and strike from flank with cavalry.

events.message: Fratricidal battle begins...
Moderates begin attack on wagon fort!
Attack fails - infantry retreats in disorder!
Warning! Noble cavalry charges from ambush!
Prokop the Great fell in battle!

objectives.primary: Hold wagon fort and destroy 50% of coalition

debriefing.victory: Prokop the Great discovered moderates' trap in time! Radicals stayed in wagon fort and repelled feigned retreat. Coalition of moderates defeated and radical Hussitism survives. History written differently...
debriefing.defeat: Tragedy at Lipany. Radicals believed feigned retreat and ran from wagon fort. Moderate cavalry struck from flank. Prokop the Great fell and with him hope of radical Hussitism. Hussite Wars end with defeat of those who began them.

phases.name: Stalemate
phases.description: Both sides behind wagon fort, negotiations fail.

events.message: Fratricidal battle begins...

phases.name: Feigned attack
phases.description: Coalition sends infantry in seemingly desperate attack.

events.message: Moderates begin attack on wagon fort!
Attack fails - infantry retreats in disorder!

phases.name: Trap
phases.description: Radicals leave fort and pursue. Cavalry strikes from flank!

events.message: Warning! Noble cavalry charges from ambush!

phases.name: Destruction of radicals
phases.description: Radicals encircled, bloody slaughter.

events.message: Prokop the Great fell in battle!

sion_1437.name: Siege of Sion Castle
sion_1437.description: Last resistance of Hussitism. Jan Roháč of Dubá defends his small castle against royal superiority.
sion_1437.historicalSignificance: End of Hussite Wars. After fall of Sion, 52 defenders were executed in Prague including Jan Roháč.

briefing.hussites: You're Jan Roháč of Dubá, last unconquered Hussite commander. You resisted siege for four months, but now Hungarian reinforcements arrived. Defend Sion to last man!
briefing.crusaders: King Sigismund loses patience. With Hungarian reinforcements finally capture that cursed castle and take Roháč alive!

reinforcements.crusaders: Hungarian reinforcements of Michal Országh arrived!

events.message: Four months of siege. Ptáček hesitates with decisive assault - Roháč is his uncle...
Defenders suffer from lack of water. Well missing in castle!
King Sigismund loses patience. Sends Hungarian army!
Michal Országh brings Hungarian knights! Situation desperate.

events.text: Hungarian knights encourage royal army to decisive assault!

events.message: Walls crumble under gun fire! Hold on!

events.text: Some defenders lose hope. Jan Roháč encourages them to fight!

events.message: Enemy penetrates through trenches!
Walls fell! Man-to-man fight in castle ruins.
It's over... But memory of Sion will never die.

debriefing.victory: Incredible! Jan Roháč and his faithful held until dusk. Under cover of night part of garrison escaped. Roháč lives and becomes legend - symbol of unbroken resistance. Hussite spirit will never die!
debriefing.defeat: Sion castle fell. Jan Roháč was captured during lunch, not expecting such rapid Hungarian attack. Together with 52 defenders he was taken to Prague. On September 9, 1437 they were all executed in Old Town Square. Roháč hung highest - on golden chain. Hussite Wars ended on gallows.

phases.name: Futile siege
phases.description: Ptáček's army tries to break through, but walls hold.

events.message: Four months of siege. Ptáček hesitates with decisive attack - Roháč is his uncle...
Defenders suffer from lack of water. Castle has no well!
King Sigismund loses patience. Sends Hungarian army!

phases.name: Arrival of Hungarians
phases.description: Hungarian reinforcements change balance of power.

events.message: Michal Országh brings Hungarian knights! Situation desperate.

events.text: Hungarian knights encourage royal army to decisive attack!

phases.name: Final assault
phases.description: General assault on walls. Defenders fight for survival.

events.message: Walls crumble under cannon fire! Hold on!

events.text: Some defenders lose hope. Jan Roháč encourages them to fight!

events.message: Enemy penetrates through trenches!

phases.name: Fall of Sion
phases.description: Last resistance. Every fallen defender is hero.

events.message: Walls fell! Man against man fighting in castle ruins.
It's over... But memory of Sion will never die.

horice_1423.name: Battle of Hořice
horice_1423.description: Žižka and Diviš Bořek with Orebite infantry and cavalry face Catholic nobility on Gothard hill. Battle without wagon fort - pure field battle.
horice_1423.historicalSignificance: Decisive defeat of Catholic nobility in northeastern Bohemia. Hussites captured Catholic wagons and guns.

briefing.hussites: Take advantageous position on Gothard hill. You have no wagons, but hill provides natural defense. Catholic nobility under Čeněk of Wartenberg approaches with cavalry superiority. Use terrain and firearms!
briefing.crusaders: Hussite heretics fortified on hill without wagons. You have numerical superiority in cavalry - crush them before they form up!

events.message: Žižka: 'Up the hill! Hold slopes, shooters forward!'
Catholic nobility forms for attack at foot of hill.
Čeněk of Wartenberg: 'Forward! Crush heretics!'
Heavy cavalry hits Hussite infantry! Attack stalls on steep slope.

events.text: Cavalry can't overcome steep slope and pikes!

events.message: Hussite howitzers and shooters mow down attackers!
Arnošt Flaška fell in battle!

events.text: Death of Arnošt Flaška shook Catholics.

events.message: Žižka: 'Now! Forward, for the chalice!'
Catholics take flight! Čeněk flees with handful of men!
All Catholic wagons and guns captured!
Čeněk of Wartenberg fled. Hussite victory complete.

debriefing.victory: Decisive victory on Gothard! Orebites under Žižka and Diviš Bořek proved they can defeat cavalry superiority even without wagon fort. Čeněk of Wartenberg lost all wagons and guns which Hussites captured. Catholic nobility in northeastern Bohemia is broken.
debriefing.defeat: Catholic superiority broke through. Gothard hill fell and with it hope of holding eastern Bohemia. Hussite forces scattered and Čeněk of Wartenberg celebrates victory.

phases.name: Taking positions
phases.description: Hussites fortify on Gothard hill, Catholics gather.

events.message: Žižka: "To the hill! Hold slopes, shooters forward!"
Catholic nobility forms for attack below hill.

phases.name: Frontal assault
phases.description: Čeněk of Wartenberg throws cavalry into frontal assault on hill.

events.message: Čeněk of Wartenberg: "Forward! Crush heretics!"
Heavy cavalry crashes into Hussite infantry! Attack bogs down on steep slope.

events.text: Cavalry cannot overcome steep slope and pikes!

phases.name: Three-hour battle
phases.description: Furious fighting on Gothard slopes. Catholics suffer heavy losses.

events.message: Hussite hand cannons and shooters mow down attackers!
Arnošt Flaška fell in battle!

events.text: Death of Arnošt Flaška shook Catholics.

phases.name: Hussite counterattack
phases.description: Žižka orders counterattack. Orebite cavalry and infantry charge from hill.

events.message: Žižka: "Now! Forward, for the chalice!"
Catholics break into flight! Čeněk flees with handful of men!

phases.name: Pursuit
phases.description: Hussites pursue fleeing Catholics and capture their wagons.

events.message: All Catholic wagons and guns captured!
Čeněk of Wartenberg escaped. Hussite victory is complete.

malesov_1424.name: Battle of Malešov
malesov_1424.description: Žižka's masterpiece. Blind hetman uses terrain for crushing defeat of anti-Hussite coalition.
malesov_1424.historicalSignificance: Bloodiest battle of Hussite Wars. 1,200 coalition soldiers fell versus 200 Hussites. Žižka became most powerful man in Bohemia.

briefing.hussites: Anti-Žižka coalition caught up with you at Malešov. Use slope above Bohynka stream valley. Enemy has numerical superiority, but terrain is on your side!
briefing.crusaders: We finally caught up with Žižka! He has fewer men. We'll surge into valley and crush heretics once and for all!

events.message: Jan Roháč: 'Lord hetman, we have good slope above valley. Bohynka stream covers our center.'
Jan Hvězda: 'I know these places. Valley narrow - enemy won't be able to deploy.'
Čeněk of Wartenberg: 'Attack! We'll crush blind man once and for all!'
Heavy cavalry enters narrow valley... Ranks crowd!

events.text: Cavalry loses momentum in swampy valley!

events.message: Howitzers and hand cannons fire into packed enemy ranks!
Coalition losses mount! Valley colors with blood!

events.text: Coalition army loses courage in murderous fire.

events.message: Žižka: 'Now! Down the hill! For God's truth!'
Hussite cavalry and infantry rush down slope at disoriented enemy!

events.text: Attack from hill! +15% to attack of Hussite units.

events.message: Coalition collapses! Men flee toward Malešov!
Čeněk of Wartenberg: 'Back! Everyone back!' Rear lines didn't even enter battle.
1,200 coalition soldiers fell. Hussites lost only 200 men.
Žižka controls battlefield. Road to Kutná Hora open!

debriefing.victory: Brilliant victory of blind commander! Žižka used terrain and discipline of his men for crushing defeat of coalition of Praguers and Catholics. 1,200 coalition soldiers fell, while Hussites lost only 200 men. Road to Kutná Hora open!
debriefing.defeat: Coalition overcame Žižka's defense. Taborites and Orphans suffered heavy losses. Blind commander lost reputation of invincibility and Hussite movement divided again.

phases.name: Taking positions
phases.description: Žižka recognizes terrain with help of Roháč and Hvězda. Hussites fortify on slope.

events.message: Jan Roháč: "Lord captain, we have good slope above valley. Bohynka stream covers our center."
Jan Hvězda: "I know these places. Valley is narrow - enemy won't be able to deploy."

phases.name: Coalition attack
phases.description: Anti-Žižka coalition throws cavalry into valley. Enemy cannot fully deploy.

events.message: Čeněk of Wartenberg: "To attack! We'll crush the blind man once and for all!"
Heavy cavalry enters narrow valley... Ranks crowd!

events.text: Cavalry loses momentum in marshy valley!

phases.name: Bloody valley
phases.description: Hussite fire from hill mows down attackers. Bloodiest phase of battle.

events.message: Hand cannons and handguns fire into crowded enemy ranks!
Coalition losses grow! Valley colors with blood!

events.text: Coalition army loses courage in murderous fire.

phases.name: Žižka's counterattack
phases.description: Žižka orders deadly counterattack down slope.

events.message: Žižka: "Now! Down the hill! For God's truth!"
Hussite cavalry and infantry rush down slope at disoriented enemy!

events.text: Attack from hill! +15% to Hussite units' attack.

phases.name: Coalition collapse
phases.description: Coalition army collapses. Rear units flee without fight.

events.message: Coalition collapses! Men flee toward Malešov!
Čeněk of Wartenberg: "Back! Everyone back!" Rear units didn't even enter battle.
1,200 coalition soldiers fell. Hussites lost only 200 men.
Žižka controls battlefield. Road to Kutná Hora open!

zivohost.name: Battle of Živohošť
zivohost.location: Area between Živohošť and Nový Knín

enemySide.composition: Heavy cavalry of Czech Catholic nobility

zivohost.terrain: High ground near Vltava crossing. Wagon fort was NOT used.
zivohost.outcome: Indecisive battle. Showed necessity of organized defense.
zivohost.aftermath: Indecisive battle. Showed necessity of organized defense.
zivohost.significance: Historically the FIRST major clash of the Hussite Wars. Demonstrated that pilgrims needed better organization and tactics.

quotes.text: Lord Peter rode with his squadron against the Ústí men, broke through them, and his entire cavalry squadron rode through them.

trivia: Historically the FIRST major clash of the Hussite Wars
Wagon fort was not used - it originated only later
Peter of Šternberk fell a year later at the Battle of Vyšehrad
Captured Hussites were thrown into Kutná Hora mine shafts

nekmir.name: Battle of Nekmíř
nekmir.location: Near Nekmíř fortress, 17 km NW of Plzeň

hussiteSide.composition: Infantry from Plzeň, wagons with guns and hand cannons

nekmir.terrain: Field near Nekmíř fortress. FIRST USE OF WAGON FORT in Hussite Wars.
nekmir.outcome: Hussite victory. Wagon tactics were born.
nekmir.aftermath: Hussite victory. Wagon tactics were born.
nekmir.significance: FIRST documented use of wagon fort in history. Only 7 wagons in semicircle formation proved the concept worked.

quotes.text: Žižka repelled him from the wagons and killed Hynek of Nekmíř. Then he continued his march and that night demolished three fortified strongholds.

trivia: FIRST documented use of wagon fort in history
Only 7 wagons - semicircle formation
Bohuslav of Švamberk later JOINED the Hussites!
Memorial to the first wagon fort at Nekmíř built only in 2017 - 598 years after the battle!
nekmir.reliability: Low - only one source (Old Czech Annals)

sudomer.name: Battle of Sudoměř
sudomer.location: Between Markovec and Škaredý fishponds, 14 km from Strakonice

enemySide.composition: Heavy cavalry, Hospitallers, squires of landfrieden

sudomer.terrain: Narrow dam between fishponds - Markovec filled, Škaredý muddy. KEY FACTOR - mud trapped dismounted knights.
sudomer.outcome: Hussite victory. First great demonstration of wagon tactics.
sudomer.aftermath: Hussite victory. First great demonstration of wagon tactics.
sudomer.significance: Foundation of Žižka's reputation as undefeated commander. Proved wagon fort could defeat heavy cavalry.

quotes.text: ...on the day of the Annunciation of the Virgin Mary, Lord Břeněk of Švihov, Valkoun of Adlar, and Jan Žižka with other brothers...

trivia: Žižka was one-eyed and approximately 60 years old
LEGEND about veils of Hussite women blinding knights is Piccolomini's fabrication
Henry of Hradec mortally wounded by arrow TO THE THUMB
Foundation of Žižka's reputation as undefeatable commander

vitkov.name: Battle of Vítkov

hussiteSide.composition: Shooters with hand cannons, flailmen, 3 women

vitkov.terrain: Extended ridge with steep slopes, wooden blockhouses. Narrow access path prevented use of numerical superiority.
vitkov.significance: Saved Prague from the First Crusade. Became symbol of Hussite resistance and Czech national memory.

quotes.text: And Žižka coming there would have been killed if his men had not pulled him with flails from the enemies' hands.
And the enemies seeing the sacrament and hearing the bell ringing and the mighty cry of the people, seized with tremendous fear took flight...

trivia: 3 WOMEN defended Vítkov
Battle cry 'Hrrr at them!' became Hussite motto
Equestrian statue of Žižka on Vítkov - third largest in the world
July 14 is Memorial Day of Czech Army
vitkov.reliability: High - Vavřinec of Březová was direct participant

vysehrad.name: Battle under Vyšehrad
vysehrad.location: Pankrác Plain, area around St. Pankrác church

commanders: Hynek Krušina of Lichtenburg (25 years old)
hussiteSide.composition: Praguers, Orebites, Taborites, Žatec, Louny forces

enemySide.composition: Hungarians, Germans, Silesians, Czech Catholic nobility

vysehrad.terrain: Flat plain with side ravine to Podolí. Side ravine became trap for nobility.
vysehrad.outcome: Decisive victory - 'substantially greater than at Vítkov'. Collapse of royal party.
vysehrad.aftermath: Decisive victory - 'substantially greater than at Vítkov'. Collapse of royal party.
vysehrad.significance: Destroyed backbone of Czech Catholic nobility. 25 banner lords fell. Secured Prague for Hussites.

quotes.text: [The nobility] proudly informed the king that they would go into fire even where he himself certainly would not be.

trivia: 25 BANNER LORDS of Czech nobility fell
Vyšehrad garrison honored surrender agreement
Dead lay NAKED for 3 DAYS on battlefield
Sigismund came LATE - after 8:00, when garrison was to surrender
vysehrad.reliability: High - multiple sources including Eberard Windecke

kutna_hora.name: Battle of Kutná Hora

enemySide.composition: Hungarian cavalry, German and Austrian detachments

kutna_hora.terrain: Hilly countryside, strategic Kaňk hill. Terrain enabled night escape.
kutna_hora.outcome: Hussite victory. Brilliant night breakthrough with wagon fort.
kutna_hora.aftermath: Hussite victory. Brilliant night breakthrough with wagon fort.
kutna_hora.significance: FIRST mobile artillery maneuver in history - night breakthrough. Proved blind Žižka's genius.

quotes.text: ...on the way they burned villages and raping virgins and women unto death, then murdered them...

trivia: Žižka was COMPLETELY BLIND - lost second eye during siege of Rábí
Kutná Hora citizens secretly cooperated with Sigismund and opened gates
Sigismund spent Christmas believing he won
FIRST mobile artillery maneuver in history - night breakthrough
